tips.comment: Was 2nd on rules debut at Warwick over 16f on good 19 days ago, only beaten 0.5L and staying on well at the business end. Should be wiser today after last run experience. Team Skelton bagged a bumper winner at Southwell on Monday.
Coastal Command is an interesting newcomer from the very powerful Henderson stable, with the eye-catching jockey booking of James Bowen. Related to several winners and should be ready first time.

Jena d'Oudairies is not the best of jumpers but could win her second hurdle race, having run well at Cheltenham last time in a Class 2 handicap hurdle. She should be able to give her seven-pound winner's penalty to the rest of the field here at Worcester.

The model I run suggests Mistletoe could cause an upset here. Mistletoe is very mispriced on a couple of platforms (trading 17s on Paddy Power and William Hill). Priced at 9s on B365. Mistletoe steps out with only the third highest RPR here of the 8 runner field, and all seem to carry the same weight with the exception of the current market favorite Jena d'Oudairies, who carries 9 lbs more. Mistletoe last ran 18 days ago, so has race fitness and looks to build on a decent second at Fontwell, which was a 2m 6f.

Not great form from the 6-year-old this winter, but a better run last month after coming off a 2-month break, only beaten 2 lengths when finishing second - good/soft going. Something to build on. I like the fact that his two highest RPR ratings that he has posted both came on quicker ground.

The model I run suggests Thirtyfour Thirty can cause an upset here. Not fancied by the early market but does have the significantly higher RPR of the field. Goes out carrying the second lowest weight of the field thanks to a significantly different official ranking. 8-10 lbs difference to the early market leaders should be a telling difference by the finish line.

Looks stupidly well handicapped on his overall form, despite not showing much in a good while. He's now 6 lbs below the mark he won off when trained by Lucinda Russell, winning a much better race than this, beating Dreams Of Home by a wide margin. He placed off a 10 lbs higher mark next time out, just bumping into one. He now finds himself 16 lbs lower than that mark he placed off. His last run hinted a return to the winner's enclosure is edging closer. He ran well back in 3rd place behind Jet Of Dreams, beaten 4L. If he can repeat that form here, he's very well in off his current mark.

The model I run suggests Captain Hugo can get his nose over the line first in this one. Captain Hugo steps out with the highest RPR of the field and doesn't appear to be overly penalized in the weights. Nearly all runners carry the same amount. Last ran 21 days ago, so does have race fitness, and trainers have a high RTF%.

Was 3rd on rules debut at Ludlow over 16f on good to soft 20 days ago, running on at the business end. Team Skelton had a bumper winner at Southwell on Monday. They have 2 running at Worcester today, but I think this will be placed once again.

Four starts over hurdles for the 4yo, one win, three decent runs in defeat. Not disgraced in a Grade 3 handicap last time out, when racing from 9lb out of the handicap. She likes the better ground and is now running in a class 5 handicap against older runners, but she does receive an 8lb age allowance. Top yard/jockey, more to come from this one.

The model I run suggests Pub Crawl can get over the line first here. Pub Crawl has an RPR towards the top of the order but has an official ranking that allows him to carry lighter weight. Last run 32 days ago, so has race fitness and has some form coming into this, with a prior 2nd and 4th at Sedgefield.
Had a bit of luck when winning at Warwick last time out but the 2 lbs increase doesn't look enough to stop him achieving the hat-trick here.

Admittedly, he comes into this with a bit to prove at present. His mark has dropped from 116 to 107, however. He's got ground conditions in his favor, and we know this track suits him.
He ran a cracker over CD off this mark last season, finishing a very close 2nd behind Trapista, beaten just a neck. That horse franked the form, winning again off a 7 lbs higher mark next time out.
He also placed off a 9 lbs higher mark than this, finishing 2nd behind Parisencore in the Bet365 Perth Silver Cup.
He ran okay last time out, not beaten far back in 3rd place. A repeat of that run with Harry in the plate would see him go close here.

Just six starts over hurdles for the 7yo and he now makes his chase debut. He likes the better ground. He was a 5L maiden winner last summer and a good 4th on his next start in a strong looking novice hurdle. He’s coming off a 7 month break, his handicap mark looks handy, unexposed over fences and the yard is in good form.

The model I run suggests Scene One can win this one. Lines up in this 10-runner race with the highest RPR of the field. Has the second lowest official ranking, which means he goes out carrying the second lowest weight. Tom Cannon picks up the reins, who is a trusted jockey. Scene One is also a prior distance winner and has the highest top speed on the scorecard.
Defied penalty and followed up easily enough last time and has a big chance off the HT from just 3lb higher. Won over course and distance on similar ground on penultimate start.

The 6yo returned at the start of the month, after 7 months off the track, and should be better for the run - excuses that day. He ran a few nice races in defeat last summer, in better races than this one and he’s on a much reduced mark now. He’s a previous C/D winner and loves the quicker ground.

Five of her six wins have come at this track, very well treated on the last of those. It has been a long time since she last got her head in front but she shaped with a bit of promise on her opening start of the season and could build on that here.

Given too much to do on debut, did all his best running at the end. The yard has won this race 3 times, and the handicapper drops the colt down 3 pounds. This looks like a good opportunity for Society of Honour to open his account.
Wasn't beaten far on debut when finishing second over C&D eight days ago. Should progress further today. Should be involved at the finish.

Solid run at Doncaster latest with a 2nd by less than a length in field of eleven runners. Won here at Beverley back in August last year just two pounds lighter, and seems to run quite well each time they are at this ground.

Worth a small each-way bet on her first run in 7 months. Has gone 15 runs since last winning but is a previous course and distance winner, goes on quick ground, and is from her lowest ever handicap mark.

Been in supreme form recently, rattling up a four-timer in low-level handicaps. Has a twelve-pound penalty to contend with but didn't look like stopping last time out and could still be very well handicapped. Unexposed at this sort of distance. Still looks to have plenty left in the tank, and with no other confirmed front runner, may have the run of the race again today.

The 3yo should be better for his run two weeks ago. He came to challenge 2f out, not the best track position and was outpaced. However, it was just a fourth career run. He was returning from a 6-month break. He was up against much higher-rated rivals than what he now faces in this handicap, and he has a 2lb lower mark.

Nicely bred 3yo filly. Three career runs. She was a runner-up two weeks ago in a maiden race, bumping into a smart looking winner. No answer in the final 2f but she did match the winner for the first mile and still saw the race out, in that strongly run contest. She should get a more suitable pace in this low grade handicap and she could prove to be better than her opening mark of 60.

A progressive looking 4yo filly. Runner-up in 3 of 5 AW races. Two turf runs. A close 4th of 17 during March and she then won a 17 runner handicap at the end of last month - the front two pulling clear that day. More to come from this one and a 3lb higher mark might not stop her.

Only 1-31 and yet to win a handicap, but continues to slip down the weights and has already posted a couple of good efforts at Thirsk and Catterick this spring. Below par at Brighton last time, but down another lb and will surely be striking soon.

Has a very good record here and has performed well with this jockey in the past too. Now running at a very competitive mark, down a class from the last two races. Has every chance of going well and challenging.

A wide-open, low-grade sprint where Vaunted looks great value at 25/1. He was in good form at the end of last season, and a recent run will have him spot on. He goes well here and is taken to pounce late on.

Too Darn Hot filly, whose dam was a winner over five furlongs early in her career, which bodes well for a race of this type. The yard is usually good with their two-year-olds, and this year has been no different.
Drops to his lowest ever handicap mark and has gone well on his first run the past couple of seasons. Marquand booked, looks to have a decent chance in this and has form on quick ground.

I'm going to give this one another chance in first-time cheekpieces and a first-time jockey booked who is riding out of his skin at the moment. The horse is bred to be much better than a 57-rated handicapper and is already 8lb lower than the initial handicap mark he was given last July. After that handicap debut, he was sent off at 5/2 off a mark of 64 when 3rd of 4. But with the new headgear and top jockey, I'd say that on balance he could well be the best value in the race at 14/1.

Ran well on turf debut last time and drops a pound here. Did all her best work at the finish, having been caught further back than ideal. This slightly longer trip should suit her, and this is a slightly easier race.

A mixed bag from the 4yo filly last year but showed ability on a going day. She is a previous C/D winner. Her best RPR rating came on fast ground when second over this C/D, that form boosted by the 1st, 3rd and 4th. Improvement possible after 7 months off the track. On a handy looking mark and the last four runners sent out by the yard have all finished a close second.

Winner at C&D and mark has tumbled of late after not winning for a while, but now looks very well handicapped off 47 and with a good jockey on board for the first time. Has had 2-3 months off since the last race and may well be better for the rest.

Has been running well over hurdles and fences, his latest chasing appearance being a win over course and distance at the beginning of last month. That form has subsequently been boosted by the runner-up so in with a great chance of going in again here.

The model I run suggests Zero Tolerance can win this race. Zero Tolerance has the middle-ranked RPR of the 3 runners but goes out carrying the lowest weight thanks to having a lower official ranking. It has the joint highest top speed on the card for this race and last ran 59 days ago. Jackpot Cash, the current market leader, last raced only 7 days ago, and you wonder whether the turnaround is too quick.

The model I run suggests each way on Jackhammer is the play here. Jackhammer is not fancied at all in the early market. The result of the model has largely been driven by Jackhammer having the highest RPR of the field and at 11 YO has plenty of experience. Ranked bottom in the official rankings, and goes out carrying the very bottom in terms of weights. Charlie Maggs on board claims a further 5 lbs on top of that, which brings the total weight difference to the top of the market to 2 stone 2 lbs.
Absolutely hosed up at Ffos Las last week and see no reason why this opposition presents a sterner test. Strong fancy.

The model I run suggests each way on Jet Patrol is the value bet here. There are 3 places up for grabs on some of the bookies, such as B365. Lewis Dobb on board is claiming a hefty 7 lbs, which takes the total weight carried for Jet Patrol down to 10-5. This is a significant difference to the market leader of over 1 stone over this 2m round trip. With 3 runners placing in a 7 runner race, this has to be the value bet at 15s.

The model I run suggests Dartmouth Castle should win this one. Highest RPR of the scorecard, doesn't really appear to be penalized by the weights and goes out with the best form (good 6th, where in the running until tailing off at the last).

The model I run suggests Lillistar can win what looks like a fairly open race. Lillistar has the second highest RPR ranking of the 7 runners but goes out carrying the significantly lower of the weights over this 2m 3f trip. Other runners have claiming jockeys on board, which muddies the water somewhat, but Lillistar still carries the lowest amount when lining up, taking the total weight differential into consideration.

Super unlucky to bump into Mermaids Cave at the beginning of her winning run (now 25lb higher) at Fontwell and the betting seemed to know that the eight-year-old was subsequently finished for the season.
The Jamie Snowden-trained inmate makes her return after a 334-day absence, but I doubt she will be lacking for fitness on this long journey north.
Unbelievable chance if reproducing her penultimate second.

The model I run suggests Celestial Reign can cause an upset here. Steps out with a middle-ranking RPR but goes out carrying the lowest weight of the 7 runners over this 2m 3f trip. Unlucky to be brought down in March and ran a decent 4th in April at this course. Looking to build on that here over a similar distance.

Not hard to envisage her being better than her last run (Curragh G3) when 4.75L 6th to One Look. All O'Briens were needing the run then and would be expected to come on for it. Probably better to look back to last season with a pretty easy G3 win from Giselle in 4th, who's since won the Lingfield Oaks trial by 9L. Was described last season as a massive filly and pedigree would give encouragement for the step up in trip. Looks a winnable Musidora and would be very surprised if 10/3 is still around on the day.

Three career runs for the 3yo filly, form 441 and hopefully more progress this year after a winter break. Excuses on her last start - heavy ground. Plenty to like about her second start, in Group 2 company, only beaten 2L and the 1st and 3rd from that race finished 1st and 2nd in the recent 1000 Guineas. She should be a big player in this Group 3 contest.

The Reverend looked a top prospect when easily winning at Ascot, but couldn't build on that in his next two starts. There's a lot of rain forecasted, so the juice in the ground will be in his favor. Judged on that Ascot run, a mark of 95 is still too low.
Stressfree needs to be held up as he was at Epsom in April when 3rd of 6 runners. He goes off the same handicap mark of 93 and will go close.

The trainer has been patient with the 4-year-old colt. Three career runs, form 121. His defeat was by a head in a 13-runner contest. He posted a high RPR rating when winning on his handicap debut last time out. Improvement with each run and on an upward curve. He’s had a nice 10-week break, and we might not have seen the best of him yet.

Lightly raced 4yo. Solid form last year in quality handicap races, over this 6f trip and on fast ground. A big run at the start of the month, losing by a hd in a 13 runner £52K handicap. He was coming off a 7 month break that day and you would hope he can take a step forward. Should be a big player in this handicap with Ryan Moore now taking over in the saddle.

Holkham Bay was quite unlucky at Goodwood as he was stuck behind horses which were dropping back. He got in the clear too late and was therefore given an easy ride. He loves York and will appreciate the rain. He's not obviously well handicapped, but could still be a couple of pounds too low.

Commanche Falls is slowly but surely getting back to a more reasonable mark. His run at Leicester wasn't as bad as he was drawn worst of all, and only the winner was able to get competitive from a low draw. He likes it here, and the rain can only help.

I can't see anything beating Inisherin here. Rain is forecasted, which goes against Night Raider and Elite Status. This horse won nicely on his first two starts at 6 furlongs last season, but might have been a little outclassed in his next two attempts. He's been off the track for quite some time, but Kevin Ryan often has his runners ready for this meeting. Ryan Moore is an eyecatching booking.

Just four runs last year for the 4yo colt, winning twice and can go on to better things this year. He won a Group 3 on fast ground last summer, and the 2nd, 3rd and 4th in that race were effectively quality Group 1 runners. Improvement possible after his seven month break from the track and he was a smart winner on his return last year. Should go well in this Group 2 contest.

Lightly raced 3yo filly. Two runs this year. Excuses last time out when not firing on her AW debut. Only beaten 2L on her return during March, in a very strong looking Listed contest against older runners. She wasn’t beaten far at this track last summer, on fast ground, in a Group 2 contest. She now drops into a class 3 handicap, her mark of 94 looks very handy and she’s now helped by a capable apprentice who is taking a useful 7lb off her back.

Gun Carriage is a 3-year-old son of Gun Runner ex Special Event. He was unraced as a 2-year-old and made his racecourse debut when third at 14/1 behind his stablemate Stay True 3/1 by Galileo in a 1m2f maiden at Leopardstown in April, when ridden by M Crehan (3) for Aidan O'Brien and Coolmore. He'll now be ridden by W Lordan, and the stable is in top form at the moment. He drops back here to a 1m maiden, and he may prove too strong for his rivals. I make him my Nap of the day.

The model I run suggests San Franco could cause an upset here. San Franco has the second highest RRP of the card, but goes out carrying the exact same weight as the majority of the 13 runners. Patrick Obrien picks up the reins and claims a further 4 lbs, which helps over this 2m 1f round trip.

the model I run suggests Tir Og can win this one. Steps out with the highest RPR of the field, and should be the most progressive here. The youngest runner of this 13 runner race, and goes out carrying the least weight of all involved over this 2m 1f race. Liam Quinlan picks up the reins and claims a further 3 lbs for Tir Og.
Made a decent comeback run last month after a 6-month break. Will strip much fitter for that. Gets its preferred ground today. Trip should suit.

The model I run suggests Kate Knows Best can get her nose over the line first in this race. Kate Knows Best lines up with the highest RPR of all the runners here and carries the same weight as 9 of the 11 runners. She hasn't run in a considerable length of time and probably shows with larger odds of 6.5s.

A more exposed bunch you won’t find. It might pay to side with one of the least exposed ones in Mark Fahy’s ARTHUR ROSE. This lightly raced 4 y/o filly has had 2 spins on the turf this year, both on soft ground, and hasn’t shown a whole pile. Back down in trip today and encountering faster ground, this might be a good opportunity for her to show an improvement in form. There isn’t much of a bias here, but you wouldn’t want to be drawn too high, so trap 2 offers another bit of mild encouragement. Fahy’s stable is purring along nicely, and at 16/1 I’ll chuck a penny in the well.

The model I run suggests each way on Whiskey On Ice is the value play here. 13 runner field with 3 places up for grabs. The result of this race simulation has largely been driven by Whiskey On Ice having a middle of the pack RPR, but goes out carrying considerably lower weight. The runners in general carry the same, but Paddy Hanlon picks up the reins and claims 7 lbs off Whiskey On Ice's back for this 2m 4f trip.
Love Sonnet has had three starts now and is in a handicap off a decent mark. She comes from a yard that tends to do very well here, and with Colin Keane booked, I do expect a much better effort.
Won well at Bellewstown last time out to get off the mark at the sixth attempt. The 7 lbs increase might not be enough to stop him going in again here.

The model I run suggests the value bet here is each way on Mr. Mcwhinny. There are 16 runners in this field, which means 5 places are up for grabs. Mr. Mcwhinny lines up with the highest RPR of the field, but a middle order official ranking. Subsequently, he goes out carrying near the bottom of the weights. Jack Gilligan on board claims 5 lbs, which takes his weights firmly down to the lower order and should help over this 2m 4f trip.
